name: Traumatic Brachial Plexus Injury
definition: Traumatic injury to the brachial plexus ranging from stretch/neurapraxia to rupture or root avulsion, often after high-energy shoulder/neck trauma.

investigations.principle: MRI/CT myelography and electrodiagnostics are timed according to suspected lesion and surgical planning.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, infection, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Nerve reconstruction has time-dependent windows in selected severe injuries.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Vata-neuropathy phenotype may be documented only in parallel.

patientEducation.summary: Traumatic injury to the brachial plexus ranging from stretch/neurapraxia to rupture or root avulsion, often after high-energy shoulder/neck trauma.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, major trauma, rapidly progressive weakness, suspected serious infection, sepsis, pathological instability or other listed red flags.
